---
title: "Animations"
description-meta: "Interactive pictures of supersingular isogeny graphs: random walks, growing balls, and spines."
---

Pictures of the supersingular isogeny graphs I work on. Every graph is computed from scratch (the arithmetic in $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$ and Vélu's formulas, with consistency checks), for primes up to 5000.

[Random walks](walks.qmd)
: A random walk on the 2-isogeny graph, the (2,3)-isogeny graph, and the versions with level-3 and level-5 structure. Each graph can be shown whole, folded by Frobenius, or restricted to its spine.

[Growing balls](balls.qmd)
: A ball grows around a random curve until it contains a curve and its Frobenius conjugate. That takes about $\sqrt{n}$ vertices.

[Spines](spines.qmd)
: Pictures of the $\mathbb{F}_p$-rational part of each graph, for one prime in each residue class.
